name: Cervical Disc Herniation
definition: Focal displacement of cervical disc material beyond the normal disc space that may cause neck pain, nerve-root compression or, less commonly, spinal cord compression.

typical: Neck pain with arm pain or paresthesia
Symptoms may worsen with neck movement or foraminal loading

redFlags.item: New gait disturbance or sphincter dysfunction
Major trauma, infection or malignancy features

core: Spurling and distraction tests in context
Myelopathy screen including gait and long-tract signs

investigations.principle: Imaging is not required for every uncomplicated short-duration case.
investigations.MRI: MRI is preferred when major/progressive neurological deficit, myelopathy, red flags or persistent symptoms would alter management.
investigations.radiographs: Radiographs may show alignment/degeneration but do not show disc/root compression well.

green: Education, activity modification and exercise-based rehabilitation
Specialist assessment when deficits persist or progress
amber: Epidural/injection or surgery requires individualized assessment, imaging correlation and risk review.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Greeva-shoola/Gridhrasi-like radiating phenotype may be documented descriptively; disc herniation remains a modern anatomical diagnosis.

patientEducation.summary: Focal displacement of cervical disc material beyond the normal disc space that may cause neck pain, nerve-root compression or, less commonly, spinal cord compression.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, sphincter change, severe infection/systemic illness, major trauma, vascular compromise or other listed red flags.
